command: fit --no-offset-channel [--onset-term expected|source] + diagnose, motifs 16, iterations 300, seed 42, pairs data/taptamdrum-pairs-raw-v1
findings: Removing the offset channel closes the microtiming exploit: zeroing a real tap's timing raised the score in 0/51 groups in every no-offset condition (51/51 in v1). The quantized source-copy >= copy count stays 51/51 only because the scores are now exactly equal; the tie is counted conservatively, not an exploit.

Retrieval: v1 .240/.524 -> no_offset .253/.554 -> +expected .260/.565 -> +source .415/.666 (all/matched MRR). Every condition remains below the raw onset baseline (.518/.740): the source-term alignment equals that baseline by construction, and the human-conditioned expected profile carries less signal (.358/.626) than the raw source, echoing the human benchmark's weak-shapelet result.

Gaming trade-off: the source term removes phase violations (0/51 shifts, 0/51 reversal) but raises source-onset-copy dominance to 23/51 sources; the expected term is intermediate (7/51, 2/51 phase; 11/51 copy); density inflation stays controlled (2/51) everywhere.
Artificial 1-ch probe improves in step with the union under every condition; no condition inverts the union > isolated-hand ordering.
recommendation: No model is promoted. no_offset is a strict improvement over v1. An onset term improves known-source retrieval but increases onset-copy gaming, the exact degeneracy the master plan requires controlling; whether any onset term enters the search objective must be decided with search-time controls and human judgments, not retrieval alone.
limitations: Validation-only, synthetic attacks, artificial views; retrieval gate versus the onset baseline remains failed in all conditions; participant-held-out, pretraining-overlap and perceptual gates remain open.
